hooks.text: A city-bus-sized asteroid snuck halfway inside our Moon's protective orbit.
Did astronomers spot a city-bus-sized asteroid just days before it struck?
A city-bus-sized rock passed one hundred seventy-five thousand kilometers from Earth.

title: The asteroid that snuck inside the Moon
description: Discover how a city-bus-sized asteroid named 2023 DZ2 was found just days before passing closer than the Moon.

beats.text: A city-bus-sized asteroid snuck halfway inside our Moon's protective orbit without warning.

beats.text: In February 2023, astronomers using a Canary Islands telescope spotted the unexpected cosmic visitor.
beats.visual: photograph of Isaac Newton Telescope exterior, La Palma, 2023
subjects: Observatorio de Roque de los Muchachos

beats.text: Detailed measurements revealed the rocky visitor was between forty and ninety meters across.
beats.visual: diagram of Apollo asteroid orbit, NASA, 2023

beats.text: Worse still, early math briefly listed it as a virtual impactor for March 2026.
Further tracking thankfully ruled out the collision, dropping the rock from the risk table completely.

beats.text: On March 25, the asteroid roared past at a distance of one hundred seventy-five thousand kilometers.
